_comment: Divider has no Figma component set — checked 2026-08-19 across every page. What Figma does declare is a `colors/divider` semantic group with five roles, so the component is built on those rather than on a colour invented for it. Layout comes from the Frontend's `common/dash-line`, which 46 call sites use.

_source.thickness: The Frontend renders `border-t`, which is 1px — exactly border-width.hairline.
_source.colours: The five roles are Figma's own `colors/divider` group, not chosen for this component. The tone axis is that group, one to one.
_source.spacing: Zero by default. The Frontend passes margin per call site (`my-2` and so on), so the divider owns no spacing of its own — the parent decides.

_frontend_evidence.implementation: `w-full border-t border-dashed` plus a colour class. Dashed is the default and the only style that component offers.
_frontend_evidence.solid: Figma's component tier already holds `carts-divider` and `orders-divider`, both solid, so a solid style has evidence on the Figma side even though the Frontend's component does not offer one.
_frontend_evidence.colours_used: border-grey (27) · border-disable (9) · border-grey-light (6) · border-grey-dark-green (4) · border-secondary · border-neutral-soft_light. Those are Tailwind greys — #B9B9B9 and friends — that predate this palette and appear nowhere in it, which is why the tone axis follows Figma's divider roles instead of copying them.

_verified_from.scope: every page searched for a COMPONENT or COMPONENT_SET matching divider / dash / separator / rule
_verified_from.result: VERIFIED ABSENT. Figma has no divider component. What it does have is a `colors/divider` semantic group with five roles, confirmed in the `2-semantic` collection, and two component-tier tokens (`carts-divider`, `orders-divider`). The component is built on those.
